title: Step through the loop
instruction: Go through the program step by step, like a computer. What happens on the highlighted line?
debrief: A loop with a fixed count runs exactly as many times as you say. A loop with a condition checks it at the start of every round. And when the condition never changes, the program gets stuck in an endless loop.

rounds.title: The robot drives round a pillar

steps.q: How many times do lines 2 and 3, the body of the loop, run?
steps.why: Repeat 4× means four rounds. In each round the robot does both commands of the body.

steps.q: How many squares does the robot move in total?
How many times does the robot beep?
steps.why: The beep isn't indented, so it isn't part of the loop body. It runs once, after the loop has finished.

rounds.title: A corridor of unknown length
code: repeat until in front of the wall:

steps.input: There are 3 free squares in front of the robot, then a wall.
options: just in front of the wall
it doesn't stop, it keeps going
steps.why: After three moves it is in front of the wall. That ends the loop and the robot stops.

steps.input: There are 3 free squares in front of the robot, then a wall.
steps.q: How many times is the check on line 1 made?
steps.why: Once before every round. Three times the way is free and the robot moves; the fourth time it is in front of the wall and the loop ends. Three rounds, four checks.

rounds.title: A broken traffic light
code: repeat until the light is green:

steps.input: The traffic light is broken and stays red.
options: only when the light really turns green
steps.why: The light never turns green, so the loop goes on and on. Until the light is fixed, the program is stuck waiting in an endless loop.

rounds.title: The waste bin
code: repeat until the bin is full:
throw in a piece of paper
throw in a piece of paper

steps.input: The bin is one piece of paper short of full.
steps.q: How many pieces of paper does the program throw in?
steps.why: The check happens only at the start of a round. At the start the bin isn't full, so the whole round runs: two pieces of paper. The bin overflows, and only then does the loop find out it's full.
